what_it_does: The data layer sits between transport (radios, SATCOM, 5G, DDS/IP networks) and the applications commanders touch (COP, planning, fires, intel, logistics). It (1) ingests heterogeneous feeds (radar/EO-IR tracks, PLI, Link 16 J-series, VMF, USMTF, Cursor-on-Target, STANAG 4607/4609/4676 ISR products, vehicle telemetry, logistics and enterprise records); (2) normalizes them into a shared data model or ontology (entities/tracks/tasks/objects in Anduril Lattice, object types/links/actions in Palantir Foundry, 'data products' with mandatory metadata under the Army Unified Data Reference Architecture); (3) publishes them over an event bus or pub/sub mesh with store-and-forward and conflict-free replication so nodes keep working when links are denied, degraded, intermittent or limited (DDIL); (4) exposes registries, catalogs, APIs and SDKs so third-party apps and sensors can plug in; (5) federates queries and synchronizes state across echelons, security enclaves and coalition networks; and (6) enforces tagging, access control and releasability so the same data can move from a vehicle to a division cloud to a partner network. In 2025-2026 the U.S. Army formally baselined this layer for NGC2 as an Anduril-led 'edge-to-cloud data mesh' (Lattice at the edge, Foundry as the cloud data layer) with Raft providing data/services registries, transformation tools and federation; the joint level is converging on Maven Smart System plus a CDAO 'Edge Data Mesh', and the enterprise layer (Advana, renamed War Data Platform in Jan 2026) is being rebuilt.

sub_taxonomy.name: S02a Tactical edge data mesh / pub-sub replication (DDIL-first)
sub_taxonomy.note: Entity/track/task replication across vehicles, command posts and mobile devices with store-and-forward and CRDT-style convergence. Owned today by Anduril Lattice Mesh (Army NGC2 baseline lead, CDAO $100M Edge Data Mesh OTA, Space Force SDANet), with Ditto (ATAK Edge Sync plugin, USSOCOM per company) and Raft ([R]DP synchronization claims at Lightning Surge) as the other named players. Government interest is documented in PM Mission Command's DDIL TAK data-services requirement and the DEVCOM C5ISR zero-trust 'data pillar in DDIL' RFI.

sub_taxonomy.name: S02b Cloud/enterprise data layer, ontology and semantic layer
sub_taxonomy.note: Palantir Foundry/Ontology (NGC2 cloud data layer; Army Vantage/ADP with >100k users; Maven), Advana/War Data Platform (Accenture Federal $821M integration task order, July 2026), Databricks/C3 AI on Advana. Highest lock-in: once workflows and security rules are modeled in an ontology they are expensive to move (INFERENCE).

sub_taxonomy.name: S02c Registries, catalogs, schema/format translation and federation
sub_taxonomy.note: Data and services registries, transformation and federation (Raft Data Platform in the NGC2 baseline), Army UDRA 'data product' metadata and mesh services, DoD AI memo's 30-day federated data catalogs, Tangram Flex (formal-methods interface code generation between STANAG-4586/LMCP/etc.), Picogrid Legion (vendor-neutral integration API). This is where 'custom integrations' live today.

sub_taxonomy.name: S02d Standards-based interoperability interfaces (government-owned)
sub_taxonomy.note: Cursor on Target / TAK Server and plugin pipeline (Army-led TAK Product Center), Link 16 J-series, VMF, USMTF, MIL-STD-2525, JREAP, NATO STANAGs (4586, 4607, 4609, 4676, 5636 core metadata, 4774/4778 labeling), OMS/UCI, FACE/SOSA, NSA TDF/EDH for data-centric security. The government insists on owning these interfaces (Open DAGIR, NGC2 'government-approved non-proprietary APIs', Operation Jailbreak / Right to Integrate). Largely commoditized; a startup cannot charge for the standard itself.

sub_taxonomy.name: S02e Cross-domain, tagging and releasability-aware data movement
sub_taxonomy.note: Attribute-based access control, machine-readable labels, cross-domain solutions at the edge (TACDS filters, NEWT body-worn CDS), coalition sharing via Mission Partner Environment / INDOPACOM Mission Network. Policy, not technology, is the binding constraint (GAO-25-106454; IMN 'thumb drives'). Overlaps S08 (coalition) and S09 (ATO).

sub_taxonomy.name: S02f Track/entity management and correlation across fabrics
sub_taxonomy.note: De-duplicating and correlating the same object reported through Lattice, TAK, IBCS, Link 16, Maven and partner systems, with provenance and quality signals. Government notices (C-sUAS 4-10 Hz track updates; Mar 2026 'Data Fusion Correlator' notice on SENSEI limitations) show this is still bought piecemeal. Overlaps S03 (fusion).

current_architecture.description: Three generations coexist. Legacy (still fielded): each program of record (AFATDS, TAIS, AMDWS, JADOCS, CPCE, JBC-P/MMC, DCGS-A, IBCS, GCCS-J) keeps its own data store, message formats (VMF, USMTF, Link 16, proprietary) and ATO; cross-system flow relies on bespoke adapters, CoT gateways and humans. Bridging generation (2020-2024): Army Project Rainmaker tactical data fabric, Palantir Army Vantage/ADP (~180 sources, >100k users), CDAO Advana enterprise platform, TAK/CoT as the de facto tactical interchange, ABMS Digital Infrastructure. Emerging (2025-2026): the Army's NGC2 four-layer architecture (transport, infrastructure, data, applications) with a common data layer baseline set on June 22 2026: Anduril Lattice provides the edge-to-cloud mesh, Palantir Foundry the cloud data layer, Raft the data/services registries, transformation tools and federation; apps from Onebrief, Accelint/Lyntris, Govini, Striveworks, Rune, Shift5, Microsoft, AWS and others attach through APIs; legacy PoRs are being forced to expose APIs (Operation Jailbreak / Right to Integrate, May 2026). At the joint level Maven Smart System (program of record, March 2026) and CDAO's Edge Data Mesh (Anduril, $100M OTA) are the CJADC2 cornerstone; Advana is being split into the War Data Platform. Navy Overmatch, DAF Battle Network and Space Force SDANet follow the same pattern with government software factories as integrators.

current_architecture.security_domain: Unclassified/CUI for development and enterprise readiness data; Secret (SIPR/tactical Secret enclaves) for NGC2 division data layers; Secret-releasable for MPE/IMN; SCI for intel feeds into Maven/TITAN. NGC2 prototypes drew an Army memo citing 'very high risk' security deficiencies (Reuters, Oct 3 2025; Palantir rebutted). Zero-trust target-level deadline Sept 2027 forces machine-readable tagging.
current_architecture.connectivity_dependency: Cloud tiers (Foundry, Advana, Maven) assume reachback; edge meshes (Lattice, Raft, Ditto, TAK) are designed for DDIL with local replication. Critics at Ivy Sting 5 argued treating DDIL as an edge case 'proves Anduril are still thinking like a cloud company' (LinkedIn, 2026, single practitioner opinion).
current_architecture.what_breaks_when_disconnected: Cloud-only ontologies and enterprise catalogs become stale or unreachable; cross-echelon federation queries fail; cross-domain and releasability services hosted centrally stop; track duplication and divergence grow until reconnection; AI decision aids hosted in the cloud (Maven) are unavailable to the edge. Mesh products mitigate by store-and-forward and CRDT convergence, but conflict resolution policy (who wins, which classification applies) is immature (INFERENCE).

technical_difficulty.summary: Building a pub/sub data layer with schemas, APIs and cloud sync is commodity engineering; what is hard is (1) DDIL-first replication with deterministic conflict resolution across thousands of nodes and mixed radios, (2) semantic interoperability across dozens of legacy message standards without losing fidelity ('compression-induced information loss' was a Rainmaker-era finding), (3) doing both under classification and releasability rules that must be machine-enforced (ZT deadline Sept 2027), (4) track/entity de-duplication with provenance across independently fused pictures, and (5) getting the artifact through an ATO and onto a government-controlled baseline. The incumbents' advantage is less the algorithms than the accumulated adapters (Anduril '100+ sensor types' claim; Picogrid '100+ systems'), the deployed node footprint and the ATO reciprocity.
required_expertise: Distributed systems (CRDTs, gossip/epidemic replication, store-and-forward, delay-tolerant networking)
Schema/ontology engineering and message-standard translation (CoT, Link 16, VMF, USMTF, STANAGs, protobuf/gRPC)
Data-centric security (ABAC, TDF/EDH, STANAG 4774/4778, cross-domain patterns)
Kubernetes/edge deployment on rugged compute, NixOS/immutable images, air-gapped delivery
Tactical networking realities (bandwidth budgets, radio MTU/latency, multicast)
DevSecOps and ATO evidence (SBOM, cATO, SWFT)
technical_difficulty.hardest_problem: Policy-aware convergence: making replicated state converge across DDIL partitions while every replica respects classification, releasability and role rules, and while conflicting reports of the same entity from different fabrics are reconciled with auditable provenance. No public evidence that any vendor has solved this generally; Lattice, Raft and Ditto each claim pieces (INFERENCE).
technical_difficulty.commodity_parts: Cloud data lakes, Kafka-style buses, REST/gRPC gateways, catalogs (DataHub/OpenMetadata-class), CoT parsing, Kubernetes, MQTT brokers, DDS implementations, MIL-STD-2525 rendering libraries, open-source ATAK plugins, LLM-based mapping assistants.

capital_intensity.assumptions: PoC: two founders, ATAK-CIV/CoT and open message specs, synthetic tracks, optional Foundry developer tier or Lattice SDK sandbox (access gated by an Anduril representative - may not be granted). Credible demo: a SBIR/STTR Phase I-II or NSIN/xTech path, participation in an exercise or hackathon (Jailbreak-style, PC-C, Lightning Surge) as a team-lead subcontractor, CUI handling, one cleared advisor, rugged edge kit, travel; 12-18 months. First production: hosting on Game Warden/UDS/Platform One or the team lead's environment to inherit ATO, IL5/IL6 evidence, FSO and facility clearance (or a cleared partner), 24/7 support for a division, sustainment engineers; assumes riding an existing enterprise agreement or OTA rather than a new competition. Ranges are INFERENCE from comparable startups (Picogrid $12M seed to Phase III in ~2 years; Rune $24M Series A to two NGC2 teams).

regulatory_access.prototype_with_commercial_unclassified_d: partly - CoT/TAK, STANAG-style schemas, open protobuf definitions and synthetic feeds allow a real prototype; but the government's actual schemas (NGC2 API baseline, IBCS, Maven ontology) are CUI or vendor-gated, and Lattice environments require an Anduril relationship.
regulatory_access.government_data_required: Yes for anything beyond a demo: real sensor/PoR message samples, NGC2 API specifications, unit data; obtainable only inside a sponsored event (Jailbreak, PC-C, SBIR with a TPOC) or as a team-lead subcontractor.
regulatory_access.itar_ear: Middleware itself is usually EAR-controlled software, but adapters to specific weapon/C2 systems (IBCS, Link 16 crypto-adjacent, fire control) can become ITAR technical data; a startup with a non-U.S.-person founder must get an export-control determination before touching PoR interface control documents. Requires specialist legal review; not a definitive judgment.
regulatory_access.cui_likely: Yes - interface control documents, network diagrams, exercise data are CUI at minimum; CMMC Level 2 practices expected.
regulatory_access.classified_integration_eventually: Yes - NGC2 division data layers run at Secret; Maven/TITAN feeds involve SCI; coalition variants at Secret-releasable.
regulatory_access.cleared_personnel_at_mvp: Not required for an unclassified MVP; required (Secret at least) to participate in exercise integration and production support; facility clearance needed to hold classified contracts.
regulatory_access.non_us_person_founder_note: A non-U.S.-person co-founder with equity/control triggers Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence (FOCI) review for any facility clearance, may bar SBIR/STTR eligibility (majority U.S.-owned rule) and complicates ITAR deemed-export handling of interface data; personnel clearances require U.S. citizenship, so the German founder cannot hold one until naturalized and the Indonesian founder cannot hold one at all. Mitigations to review with counsel: structure so U.S. persons hold control and cleared roles, keep the non-U.S. founder on unclassified commercial/international (NATO/EU) product lines, or pursue the German/NATO market (S08) first. Describe, do not conclude - this needs a FOCI/export attorney.

why_not_solved.explanation: For two decades each PoR and prime owned its data and interfaces; only in May 2026 did the Army run Jailbreak to force API exposure. Now the replacement is itself vendor-led (Lattice/Foundry) with SDK access gated by the vendor, so lock-in is shifting rather than disappearing.

GAO (2025) found restrictive classification the main hindrance to sharing C2 data and no owner of the problem; tagging is manual and inconsistent; the ZT data pillar deadline (Sept 2027) is the first forcing function.

Dozens of message standards with lossy translations, hundreds of sensor types, and no standard vehicle/health protocol; every new sensor or PoR is a bespoke adapter (Shift5 two months; Jailbreak needed 600 people).

Buyers split across CPE C2IN, PM MC, C5ISR, CDAO, NAVWAR, PEO C3BM, SSC, DISA and units; data-layer money is not a line item but buried in NGC2, Maven, Advana and MPE portfolios; SBIR winners (Tangram, Cougaar, Securboration) rarely reach a program.

CRDT-based offline-first sync, cheap rugged edge compute (Voyager/Menace-T), protobuf/gRPC schema registries and LLM-assisted schema mapping matured 2018-2024; the MWI article (Feb 2026) explicitly ties the 2024-2026 data-mesh awards to CRDTs.

Government prefers to own interfaces (Open DAGIR, UDRA) and to buy the fabric from a platform vendor under an enterprise agreement; a standalone middleware company has no price point between 'free government standard' and 'platform bundled by Anduril/Palantir'.

For Army division-and-below the data-layer plumbing was designated in June 2026 (Anduril/Palantir/Raft), joint fusion is Maven, tactical interchange is TAK. What remains unsolved is the seams: onboarding legacy/third-party systems, policy-aware DDIL sync, releasability tagging, cross-fabric entity reconciliation and the catalog at tactical echelons.

attractiveness.bull: The data layer is where the Army is now spending (NGC2 ~$3B FY26 portfolio, Maven $2.3B five-year request, $30B of enterprise-agreement ceilings across Anduril and Palantir) and where the government has publicly conceded the seams are unsolved: undocumented APIs (Jailbreak), classification-blocked sharing (GAO), manual tagging (ZT PfMO), thumb-drive coalition workflows (IMN), and a mesh that stops at division. Team leads (Anduril, Lockheed) actively recruit small vendors into their stacks (Rune, Shift5, Accelint, Striveworks joined within months), the TAK plugin pipeline and Tradewinds are open doors, and government-owned interface policy (Open DAGIR, R2I) means a startup that builds the conformance/adapter tooling the government wants to own can be pulled through without competing with the platform owners.
attractiveness.bear: The platform itself is taken: Anduril leads the Army baseline, Palantir owns the ontology and Maven, Raft holds registries/federation, Ditto has the CRDT niche, and all of them can absorb any adapter, catalog or sync feature a startup demonstrates. Contract values for the small players in this layer are undisclosed or SBIR-scale, several data-translation SBIR firms never transitioned, Advana shows enterprise data programs churning for years, and every meaningful integration requires CUI/Secret access, an ATO and a cleared team - a structural problem for a two-student team with a non-U.S.-person founder. Absence of a visible competitor in a sub-niche mostly reflects that the incumbents have not prioritized it yet, not an open market.
attractiveness.verdict: Medium-low for a standalone data-fabric play; medium for a narrow 'seam' product (policy-aware sync, releasability tagging, onboarding/conformance tooling, cross-fabric entity reconciliation) sold through a team lead or the TAK/Tradewinds doors, with the explicit expectation that the exit is acquisition by or licensing to a platform owner.

candidate_gaps.title: Self-service onboarding and conformance tooling for legacy systems and third-party sensors onto the government-baselined data layer
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Every new sensor, vehicle or program of record still needs a bespoke, vendor-built adapter and a human-run integration event to join the NGC2/TAK/Maven data layer, because interface documentation, schema mapping and conformance testing are not productized.
candidate_gaps.user: Program-office and unit integration cells; small vendors trying to join a team lead's stack; TAK Product Center plugin developers
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Vendor obtains ICDs or reverse-engineers messages (often CUI, often undocumented). 2) Engineers hand-write a translator to CoT/Lattice entity/Foundry object schema. 3) Integration is validated at an in-person event (Jailbreak, Ivy Sting, Lightning Surge) with firewall and ATO surprises. 4) The adapter is maintained by that vendor only; the next unit or exercise repeats the work.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Team-lead engineers (Anduril translators, Raft transformation tools), Picogrid Legion, Tangram Pro code generation, TAK plugin pipeline, manual API documentation produced at Jailbreak.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Time-to-integrate is measured in weeks to months per system (Shift5 two months; Jailbreak needed 600 people for 70 systems); no independent conformance test exists for 'is this feed NGC2-baseline compliant'; knowledge is trapped inside the platform vendor.

candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: An open, LLM-assisted schema-mapping and conformance test harness that ingests an ICD or sample messages (CoT, VMF, Link 16, STANAG 4676, protobuf) and emits a verified adapter plus a machine-readable conformance report against a target schema (Lattice entity, Foundry object type, UDRA data-product metadata), runnable in an air-gapped lab.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Open-source CLI/service that maps CoT/STANAG 4676/VMF samples to Lattice SDK entity protobufs and back, with property-based conformance tests and a report; demonstrated on ATAK-CIV plus a public Lattice SDK sandbox or a mock; then a Jailbreak 1.5 / xTech entry.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Public message specs and synthetic data for MVP; real ICDs (CUI) and exercise message captures for credibility.
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: TAK Server, Lattice SDK (gated), Foundry OSDK, Raft registry APIs (not public), at least one PoR via a Jailbreak-style event.
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: Army xTech / SBIR Phase I-II, TAK plugin pipeline, Tradewinds video, Jailbreak 1.5 participation, subcontract to a team lead.
candidate_gaps.why_now: June 2026 baseline creates a target to conform to; R2I plans an API marketplace; DoD AI memo mandates federated catalogs; enterprise agreements make integration cost, not licensing, the Army's marginal expense.
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Government or platform owner builds it as a free capability; startup cannot access the real schemas without being inside a team.

candidate_gaps.title: Policy-aware DDIL data synchronization (classification- and releasability-respecting CRDT replication) as a vendor-neutral component
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Edge meshes can replicate data through outages, but no public product converges replicated state while enforcing per-attribute classification, releasability and role rules across partitions and across two vendors' fabrics.
candidate_gaps.user: Division/brigade data-layer administrators, coalition tactical MPE operators, ZT program offices
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Data is replicated within one vendor mesh (Lattice, Raft, Ditto) with vendor-specific conflict rules. 2) Cross-enclave or cross-partner movement goes through a CDS or is re-entered by hand on the releasable enclave. 3) After reconnection, duplicates and stale objects are cleaned manually or ignored.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Anduril Lattice Mesh, Raft [R]DP sync, Ditto CRDTs, TAK Server federation; CDS guards (TACDS, NEWT) at boundaries.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Convergence and policy are handled by different products; releasability markings do not aggregate by dominance, so guards apply the most restrictive rule and data is lost or delayed; each mesh is proprietary so two fabrics cannot converge.

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: Requires simultaneous depth in CRDT theory, tactical radios and DoD labeling policy (TDF/STANAG 4774/4778) plus classified test access; the two obvious owners (Anduril, Ditto) have solved sync but not policy, and policy people do not build databases.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: High from Anduril and Ditto; medium from CDS vendors. A vendor-neutral library that both fabrics could embed is defensible only if adopted as a government standard (OpenTDF-style).
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: Label-carrying CRDT types (each field carries TDF-style attributes) with replication filters derived from ABAC policy so a node only ever holds and forwards what its clearance/releasability allows, plus deterministic merge with provenance; packaged as an open library for TAK Server and as a Lattice/Foundry-adjacent service.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Open-source labeled-CRDT library integrated with ATAK-CIV/TAK Server federation, demonstrated across three partitions with US-only, REL-FVEY and REL-NATO labels on synthetic data; measure convergence, leakage (zero) and bandwidth.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Synthetic labeled data for MVP; real labeling policy (CAPCO/ISM, STANAG 4774) and exercise captures later.
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: TAK Server, Lattice SDK, CDS vendors, MPE/IMN enclaves.
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: DEVCOM C5ISR RFI follow-on/SBIR, DoD CIO ZT PfMO pilots, NATO DIANA (data-centric security), TAK plugin pipeline.
candidate_gaps.why_now: Sept 2027 ZT deadline, two funded data-mesh prototypes needing interoperability, Five Eyes/NATO Maven and Overmatch arrangements creating multi-releasability traffic.
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Policy, not technology, is the binding constraint (IMN: 'policy has to dictate what we're actually allowed to do'); a non-U.S.-person founder cannot work on classified labeling data.

candidate_gaps.title: Automated, machine-readable data tagging and releasability at the point of production (tactical and coalition)
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Tagging is manual, inconsistent and negotiated by phone over weeks, so data produced at collateral Secret cannot flow to allies or across systems even when policy would allow it.
candidate_gaps.user: Intel analysts and staff producing products; foreign disclosure officers; MPE administrators; ZT program offices
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Producer creates product in a national system with default classification inheritance. 2) To share, staff re-create it on the releasable enclave (WFX 24-03) or hand-carry via CDS. 3) Tagging vocabularies differ by community; access rules are negotiated manually.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Human FDOs, CAPCO markings, CDS guards, MPE lower enclaves, Anchor Defense-style tagging content, NSA TDF standard.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Terms used 'cavalierly', no interoperable machine rules, 'weeks of negotiation'; releasability does not aggregate by dominance, forcing most-restrictive handling.

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: Requires classified data access, security-policy expertise and buy-in from disclosure authorities; commercial data-governance vendors (Immuta, Virtru) target enterprise IT not tactical enclaves; the market is small and policy-gated.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: Medium: Palantir and Anduril already implement marking-aware access inside their platforms; CDS vendors could add ML tagging. Cross-vendor, standard-based tagging is the only defensible angle.
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: ML-assisted tagging at ingest that emits STANAG 4774/4778 and TDF-conformant labels with confidence and rationale, plus a controlled-vocabulary service mapping community terms, integrated into TAK Server and the NGC2 data layer so releasable subsets are generated automatically.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Prototype on unclassified/synthetic reports: classify and label CoT and free-text reports, generate REL-subset objects, run through an open-source guard simulation; measure FDO review time saved.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Unclassified marking guides and synthetic corpora initially; classified security classification guides and real products only with a sponsor.
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: TAK Server, CDS vendors, MPE/IMN, Foundry/Lattice access-control APIs.
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: DoD CIO ZT pilots, DISA MPE 'starting small' demos, Army MI innovation cells, NATO DIANA.
candidate_gaps.why_now: Sept 2027 ZT deadline; MPE going data-centric by 2027; coalition Maven/Overmatch expansions; DoD AI memo directing removal of data-sharing blockers.
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Disclosure authorities may never accept machine-generated releasability decisions; the founding team cannot access classified guides; a non-U.S.-person founder is a direct conflict with the mission.

candidate_gaps.title: Cross-fabric entity reconciliation, provenance and catalog ('fabric of fabrics') across Lattice, Foundry/Maven, TAK, IBCS and coalition systems
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: The same object reported through several independently fused pictures becomes duplicate or conflicting tracks with no auditable provenance, and there is no tactical-echelon catalog that tells a consumer which data product to trust.
candidate_gaps.user: Battle captains and air-defense/C-UAS operators; data-layer administrators; UDRA data stewards
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Each fabric fuses its own tracks. 2) Bridges (CoT gateways, Link 16 forwarders) re-inject tracks into other systems creating duplicates. 3) Operators mentally de-duplicate or a 'Data Fusion Correlator' is bought per program. 4) Catalogs exist at enterprise level (Advana, Vantage) but UDRA data products at lower echelons are by exception only.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Vendor-internal correlation (Lattice, IBCS, Maven), JFN object-based common data layer, government 'Data Fusion Correlator' buys, Raft registries in the NGC2 baseline.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: No cross-vendor track identity or provenance model; quality signals and feedback loops absent (UDRA 'Diet Coke' analogy: no labeling, quality or anti-tamper indicators); enterprise catalog connected sources without agreements (IG on Advana).

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: Correlation across proprietary fabrics needs access to each vendor's entity model and to classified track data; the platform owners each prefer to be the single fabric; catalogs are unglamorous.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: High: Raft's baseline role covers registries and federation; Anduril owns the entity model. Defensible only as an independent quality/provenance auditor the government wants to own.
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: A provenance and identity-resolution service that assigns cross-fabric stable IDs to entities, records lineage and quality metrics per producer, and publishes a UDRA-conformant catalog usable at brigade/division on edge compute.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Ingest CoT from TAK and entities from a Lattice sandbox or mock, resolve duplicates with configurable rules, expose a catalog with quality scores and lineage; demo at a C-UAS-themed hackathon.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Synthetic multi-source tracks; later real exercise captures (CUI/Secret).
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: Lattice SDK, TAK Server, Raft registry APIs, JFN/IBCS interfaces (not public).
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: JIATF-401 CSO, xTech hackathon (sensor integration problem area), Tradewinds, DIU Blue Object Management Challenge follow-ons.
candidate_gaps.why_now: Multiple funded fabrics now coexist (Lattice, Foundry, Raft, Maven, JFN) and must interoperate; C-UAS urgency; catalog mandate.
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Becomes a feature of Raft or Lattice; overlaps S03 fusion vendors; access to classified track data.

saturation_statement: Research appears near saturation for what is reachable under this session's constraints because: (1) the same primary facts (June 22 2026 baseline; Anduril/Palantir/Raft roles; the $10B and $20B enterprise ceilings; the $100M Edge Data Mesh OTA; Maven PoR; Advana/WDP churn; UDRA v1.0) recur across independent mirrors with consistent dates and numbers; (2) the government-side pain evidence converges from four unrelated sources (GAO, DoD CIO ZT PfMO, INDOPACOM, Army UDRA RFI and Jailbreak) on the same seams - undocumented interfaces, classification/releasability, tagging, and a mesh that stops above the tactical echelon; (3) additional GitHub queries on Raft/DAF, SBIR data-fabric awards and Cursor-on-Target fabric integration returned nothing new, indicating the public record on small-vendor traction in this layer is thin rather than unsearched. Gaps that a later stage should close with direct access: Raft's funding and contract values; obligations under the Palantir and Anduril enterprise agreements (USAspending); the FY2026-FY2027 Army and CDAO justification-book lines for the data layer; the text of the Common Data Fabric RFI (Dec 2024) and PM MC RFIs; Ditto's actual DoD contracts; and DOT&E/GAO assessments of NGC2 data-layer performance at PC-C6.
